newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan mulls burden-sharing for NCB units - sources.
newsitem.headline: Japan mulls burden-sharing for NCB units - sources.

text.p: Japanese financial institutions may need to share the burden of losses at three troubled financial affiliates of Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) in accordance with the amount of their outstanding loans to the units, banking sources told Reuters on Monday.
The Finance Ministry has unofficially floated the idea of burden-sharing by creditor banks in accordance with the amount of their outstanding loans, the sources said.
As the scale of problem makes it hard for NCB to tackle it alone, creditor banks would halt collection of loans to the units, which in effect would mean they would absorb losses, the sources said.
If the parties concerned were to reach agreement, the creditors' businesses could be adversely affected, said the banking sources, who did not want to be identified.

NCB's three troubled non-bank financial affiliates have total borrowings of some 1.9 trillion yen, which mostly date from the 1980s "bubble" era of inflated asset prices, and a majority of the loans are now non-performing loans, the sources said.

Of the total, outstanding loans made by trust banks to the NCB units totalled 430 billion yen and those by agricultural financial firms stood at 240 billion yen. Loans by Japanese major "city" banks totalled 370 billion yen and by long-term credit banks, including NCB itself, totalled 360 billion yen, the sources said.
